text:
Abstract
We asked whether GEO accession GSE309890 is the same record as GDS309890. To answer this, we queried NCBI GEO with two steps: accession resolution to numeric UIDs and record retrieval with file listings. We used geo_resolve_accession to map “GSE309890 GDS309890” to UIDs and identify official page and FTP locations, then geo_series to fetch each record’s metadata and supplementary files. GSE309890 resolved to UID 200309890 and retrieved as a GEO Series with 6 samples, platform GPL24659, organism Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655, and one supplementary file (CSV, 510K). GDS309890 resolved to UID 309890 as a GEO curated DataSet, but its metadata fields were empty in the esummary response and no FTP directory or files were registered. These results show the accessions are different record types with distinct UIDs and paths; GSE309890 is the Series containing the processed data files, while GDS309890 is a separate DataSet record that currently does not provide files in this query. Clarifying this distinction matters for data retrieval: processed expression values for this study must be downloaded from the GSE309890 supplementary directory, not from GDS309890.

I. Introduction
Background. NCBI GEO indexes multiple record types: Series (GSE) as the primary unit for expression studies, Samples (GSM), Platforms (GPL), and curated DataSets (GDS). End users often need to distinguish whether different accessions refer to the same data source or different layers of curation.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same GEO record and where the usable expression files reside.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 are the same record and identify which holds downloadable processed data. Hypothesis: they are distinct record types with different UIDs and only the GSE record provides supplementary files for this study.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We resolved both accessions to numeric UIDs and record types, then retrieved Series/DataSet metadata and file listings. GEO’s accession resolver provides canonical page and FTP URLs; GEO Series retrieval lists supplementary files, which are the only location for processed values.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO via functions.geo_resolve_accession and functions.geo_series.
Procedures.
- functions.geo_resolve_accession with accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890".
- functions.geo_series with accession="GSE309890", list_files=true.
- functions.geo_series with accession="GDS309890", list_files=true.
Statistical Analysis. Counts were read directly from returned fields:
- sample_count from the GSE309890 record (n=6).
- supplementary_files count from the listed files arrays (GSE309890: 1; GDS309890: 0).
No deduplication was required. Proportions were not computed.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1. GEO accession comparison for GSE309890 vs GDS309890.

| Field | GSE309890 | GDS309890 |
|---|---|---|
| Entry type / label | GSE / Series | GDS / curated DataSet |
| UID | 200309890 | 309890 |
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback | (empty in response) |
| Organism (taxon) | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | (empty in response) |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | (empty in response) |
| Platform | GPL24659 | (empty in response) |
| Sample count | 6 | (empty in response) |
| GEO page URL | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890 | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890 |
| FTP directory URL | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/soft/ (reported missing) |
| Supplementary directory | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/ | (no directory present) |
| Supplementary files (count) | 1 | 0 |
| Supplementary file URL(s) | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | — |
| PubMed links | none registered | none registered |

Findings.
- GSE309890 and GDS309890 have different UIDs (200309890 vs 309890) and different entry types (Series vs curated DataSet).
- GSE309890 lists 6 samples and one supplementary file (CSV; 510K).
- GDS309890 returned no metadata fields and registered no files or FTP directory in this query.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. GSE309890 is not the same record as GDS309890. The Series (GSE309890) is the primary record carrying the study’s processed data files, while the curated DataSet (GDS309890) is a separate accession that currently does not provide files in this response.
Context. The accession resolver returned distinct UIDs and canonical URLs for each accession. The Series record included platform, organism, and sample count, and listed one downloadable CSV file. The DataSet record’s esummary was empty for the fields queried and the reported FTP path did not exist, indicating no registered downloadable content through that path in this call.
Limitations. GEO’s API returns metadata only; processed values exist solely in the supplementary files. The GDS record shown here did not return metadata or files; some GDS records exist only as curation layers and may not mirror every Series. No PubMed link was registered for either accession in these GEO records.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are different GEO records. To obtain processed expression data, use the GSE309890 supplementary directory. A next query worth running is a GEO search for any curated DataSets linked to this Series or a broader GDS search to identify if a populated GDS exists for this study.

References
[1] NCBI GEO accession resolver: GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO accession resolver: GDS309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[3] GSE309890 Series FTP directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[4] GSE309890 supplementary directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[5] GSE309890 supplementary file (FPKMs). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[6] GDS309890 FTP path reported (no directory present). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/soft/
[7] E-utilities esummary endpoint used for GSE/GDS queries. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI GEO and NCBI E-utilities for data access.
